meta.source: BUI Know Your Product (KYP) workbook, restructured pass 2
meta.note: This is a restructuring + enrichment pass over the original 156-item KYP extraction. Three kinds of change were made to every item: (1) DEDUP -- near-duplicate entries that the original free-text parser had split apart (same physical part described twice at different confidence scores, or a generic 'parent' entry duplicating a specific sibling item) were merged; merged items carry a 'merged_from' field listing what was folded in. (2) RESTRUCTURE -- concrete spec options and business rules (grades, dimensions, materials, MOQs) that used to live only in free-text 'notes' were moved into 'required_attributes' as part of the actual ask-instruction, so notes now hold only background/context, not actionable spec detail. (3) ENRICH -- aliases were extended with genuine Indian trade/vernacular terms and global/international milling-industry terminology, drawn from general domain knowledge rather than the sheet alone. 5 items are entirely new (not present in the original KYP sheet at all) and are flagged added_from_domain_knowledge=true -- these are well-established parts in the flour-milling trade but have NOT been verified against BUI's actual stock, so confirm them before publishing. Every other alias/attribute addition is general industry terminology, not fabricated specifics -- no invented dimensions, grades, or part numbers were added anywhere; only real numbers already present in the original sheet were restructured.

schema.aliases: list[string] -- alternate names, including Indian trade/vernacular terms and global/international technical synonyms
schema.required_attributes: list[string] -- everything needed to correctly identify, spec, and quote the item: dimensions, materials, variant options with their real values, MOQ/pack-size rules, compatibility questions
schema.notes: list[string] -- background/context only: what the part is, where it's used, why it matters, distributor/brand info, common points of confusion. No 'ask ___' instructions live here anymore.
schema.match_confidence: float 0-1, or null for items added outside the original KYP sheet
schema.merged_from: optional list[string] -- present only on items formed by merging duplicate source entries
schema.added_from_domain_knowledge: optional bool -- present and true only on items with no original KYP source at all

general_notes: Sieve & Pan Cleaners (subcategory): loose objects that sit on top of or below the sieve mesh inside a plansifter compartment and bounce/vibrate to stop flour from blinding (clogging) the mesh. Across this whole subcategory, the plansifter make matters because compartment/screen depth decides which size fits, and it is genuinely hard to tell several of these apart over the phone -- always offer to send or request a reference picture.

required_attributes: Ask grade and the number within the grade -- 4 grade families exist: GG (6 GG to 74 GG), XXX (3 XXX to 17 XXX), MF (3 MF to 13 MF), N / double-X (3 N to 25 N)
Ask fabric family: standard sieving fabric, Milling Forte (heavier thread, same opening, longer life), or heavy-duty XXX grade -- trade-off is service life vs open (sifting) area
Ask width: 3 standard widths stocked -- 115 cm, 136 cm, 158 cm
Ask length in meters -- priced and ordered per meter
Ask the plansifter make -- frame/stretching sizes differ by machine (1250x1250 mm and 1500x1500 mm are common)

Ask the micron opening if the client knows it; if not, ask what flour it is sifting (maida, suji/rava, chokar/bran) so the opening can be matched to the product, since spec is really driven by micron opening rather than the grade number alone
If the client is unsure of the grade, request a picture or a physical swatch of the old cloth
notes: Authorized distributor for Sefar Nytal (Swiss brand) in India -- this is the reference brand for bolting cloth in Indian roller flour mills
'Resham ki jali' (literally 'silk mesh') is the common bazaar/vernacular name even though the fabric is nylon, not silk -- a holdover from when sieving cloth genuinely was silk

required_attributes: Ask diameter and length in inches, being clear whether it is flat diameter or actual (inflated) diameter -- these two numbers are different and easy to mix up

If the client has a specific fabric or the exact old sleeve, request a picture or a sample -- easy to send the wrong size without one
notes: Flexible connector that joins plansifter sections/spouts together -- nylon elastic filter fabric with HDPE/nylon support rings and an elastic strip at both ends for tool-free fitting

general_notes: Elevator Buckets (subcategory): covers both bucket profiles sold -- AA Type (double-A, default shape when the client doesn't specify) and Shovel Type (deeper scoop). For metal buckets (MS/SS), thickness is asked in gauge: 18, 16, 14, 12, or 10 gauge.

Conveyor Belts (subcategory): the full range of belt materials stocked is black rubber, white/food-grade rubber, cotton, nylon-cotton, polyester, PVC, PU, yellow nylon, hair (camel-hair transmission), and sandwich (two-colour, different top/bottom) belting. See the individual belt items below for material-specific thickness options; all are ultimately asked for width, length (in feet or meters), open-end vs endless, and quantity.

Jointing Accessories (subcategory): fasteners and hardware used to join conveyor belt ends and fix elevator buckets to the belt -- see Bucket Bolt, Nylock Nut, Belt Fastener, and Special Conveyor Belt Fasteners below.

general_notes: Bearing (subcategory): where possible, always ask for the bearing number stamped on the old bearing (e.g. 6205, 32210, 22218) first -- it is the fastest and most reliable way to match exactly, faster than working back from bore/OD/width dimensions.

Coupling (subcategory): couplings join two shafts that are often different diameters -- always ask both shaft (bore) sizes, not just one, and ask for the size/model number off the old coupling where possible.

Chain & Chain Sprocket (subcategory): chain and sprocket must be quoted together against the same pitch/number -- always confirm simplex (single row), duplex (double row), or triplex (triple row) before quoting, since it is easy to mix these up over the phone. Standard chain pitches are 1/2 in, 3/8 in, 5/8 in, and 1 in; a packet of chain is conventionally 3 m (about 10 ft) and is sold in packets, not by the meter.
Pulleys (subcategory): see Flat Belt Pulley, Plain Bore V Belt Pulley, Taper Bush V Belt Pulley, and Timing Pulley below.
